newsitem.title: USA: Gay Head, Mass., votes to change name to Aquinnah.
newsitem.headline: Gay Head, Mass., votes to change name to Aquinnah.

text.p: Residents of one town on the resort island of Martha's Vineyard decided to change the municipality's name from Gay Head to Aquinnah.
The name change, which must still be approved by the Massachusetts Legislature, was supported by members of the Wampanoag Indian tribe which makes up about half the town's population.
A count of Wednesday's voting showed the measure passed 79 to 76.
Early explores gave the name Gay Head to the colorful cliffs on the western tip of the Island off of Cape Code. The tribe called the cliffs Aquinnah, which means "land under the hill."
The town adopted the name Gay Head as its official name when it was incorporated in 1870.
Residents six years ago voted 89-36 against the name change, but backers of the measure said the times have changed.
